title: Machine learning guided XylM variant improved biosensor-indicated productivity
summary: Two machine-learning-assisted directed-evolution cycles produced XylM-D140E-V144K-F243L-N244S, reported to have 15-fold higher 3-methylsalicylic acid productivity than wild-type XylM. Productivity was estimated using XylS-dependent fluorescence in a sensor strain; this is a biosensor-based productivity readout, not a purified-enzyme kinetic constant.
ai_technology: Machine-learning-assisted directed evolution using biosensor-derived activity data
organization: The University of Tokyo; National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology; AIST-Waseda University Computational Bio Big-Data Open Innovation Laboratory

source_review.scope: Primary ACS publisher indexed abstract and affiliation/article-history metadata, cross-checked against primary PubMed abstract and metadata.

evidence.tested: The publisher reports XylM-D140E-V144K-F243L-N244S with 15-fold greater 3-methylsalicylic-acid productivity than wild type after two ML-assisted directed-evolution cycles, using XylS-dependent fluorescence from a sensor strain as the measured indicator.
evidence.unknown: The signal is an indirect biosensor-based productivity proxy; the reported value is not a purified-enzyme kinetic constant.
evidence.ai_role: Machine learning used sensor-derived data to guide two rounds of directed evolution and prioritize XylM variants.
